Hidden by the chip: reads as zeros
Hidden by the chip: it always reads as 00 00 00 00, so the real value can never be read back.
No role is known for this page.
The unique serial number of the chip and its check bytes. Written at the factory and never changeable.
Bytes 2 and 3 of page 2 lock pages 3 to 15. Each bit can only go from 0 to 1, so locking is permanent.
Tells readers this is an NFC Forum tag and how much NDEF memory it has. Bits here can only be set, never cleared.
The NDEF message lives here, framed by TLV markers: 03 starts it and FE ends it. NTAG213 starts with a Lock Control TLV (01 03 A0 0C 34) that must be kept.
Lock bits for the pages from 16 onwards. Like the static lock bytes, a bit set to 1 is permanent.
Configuration. Byte 3 is AUTH0: the first page that needs the password. The default FF means no protection.
Access settings. Bit 7 (PROT) chooses whether reading also needs the password; the low bits limit failed attempts.
The 32-bit password. The chip never gives it back: this page always reads as zeros.
The password acknowledge sent after a correct password. It also always reads as zeros.
The 16-bit one-way counter of the Ultralight C. It can only count up.
AUTH0 / AUTH1 of the Ultralight C: the first page that needs authentication and whether reading needs it too. Tag Forge never changes them.
The Ultralight C authentication key. The chip never lets it be read, so it always shows as zeros.
The last block of every MIFARE Classic sector: Key A, access bits and Key B. Tag Forge reads the rest of the card but never writes this block, because a wrong value can lock the sector for good.
Hold the tag you want to copy. Tag Forge only reads it; the source is never written.
Only between tags of the same chip model. Keeps data outside the NDEF message. Pages 0 to 3, lock bytes and configuration are never copied.
Copies the readable data blocks only. Sector trailers (keys and access bits) and block 0 are never written.

%1$d data blocks copied and verified. Sectors skipped because they need a private key: %2$d.

Works with NTAG21x, the MIFARE Ultralight family and NTAG210/212 (direct NfcA access), ISO 15693 (dump), MIFARE Classic (phones with an NXP chip, public keys only) and any NDEF tag through Android. FeliCa, NfcB and ISO 14443-4 cards are information only unless they hold NDEF. When a tag does not support a tool, the tool tells you why.
